subject: general
question: Pipe A, pipe B and pipe C together can fill a tank in 20 minutes, but because of the leak all three pipes take 10 minutes more time to fill the tank completely. Find the time in which leak can empty the full tank.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Combined **efficiency** of (A+B+C) = 1/20 units/min.

Combined **efficiency** with **leak** = 1/(20 + 10) = 1/30 units/min.

Leak efficiency = 1/20 − 1/30 = (3 − 2)/60 = 1/60 units/min.

Time to empty = 60/1 = 60 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time = 20 min, Time with leak = 20 + 10 = 30 min.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 3 units/min

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B + C + Leak) = 2 units/min

⇒ Efficiency of Leak = Efficiency of (A + B + C + Leak) − Efficiency of (A + B + C)

⇒ Efficiency of Leak = 2 − 3 = −1 unit/min (Negative sign denotes emptying)

⇒ Time taken by **Leak** to empty the tank = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Leak

⇒ Time = 60 ÷ 1 = 60 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 60 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Efficiency

Filling pipes have **positive efficiency** while emptying pipes or leaks have **negative efficiency**.

Net Work Formula

Total Time = 1 / (1/T₁ + 1/T₂ − 1/Tₗₑₐₖ) where T represents individual time taken by each component.

Time and Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete a specific task (Work = Efficiency × Time).</p
